chunks: Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Muzaffar Al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud narrated to us, from his father, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Ishkeeb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abdul-A'la, who said: I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both)

about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'So, avoid the filth of idols and avoid false speech.' He said: The filth from idols is chess, and false speech is singing. I said: His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'And among the people is he who buys amusement of speech.' He said: From it is singing.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'filth of idols' refer to in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) offers a specific exegetical interpretation (*tafsir*) linking the Quranic command to 'avoid the filth of idols' to the game of chess (*al-shatranj*), which was prevalent in early Islamic society. He further identifies 'false speech' and 'amusement of speech' (*lahw al-hadith*) with singing (*al-ghana'*), establishing a theological basis for its prohibition in Shia jurisprudence. This hadith is pivotal in the scholarly discourse on *lahw* (frivolity) and the spiritual impurity of specific cultural entertainments.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Mudaffar bin Ja’far bin Mudaffar al-Alawi, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ja’far bin Muhammed bin Mas’ud, from his father, that he said: We were told by Hussain bin Ishkeeb, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Surri, from Hussain bin Sa’eed, from Abu Ahmad, Muhammed bin Abi ‘Umayr, from Ali bin Abi Hamza, from Abdul-A’la, that he said: I asked Ja’far bin Muhammed, peace be upon them both,

about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «So, avoid the filth of idols and forged statement» [22:30]. He said: Filth from idols is chess, and forged speech is singing. I said: The saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And among the people is the one who buys amusement of speech» [31:6]. He said: From it is singing.
